question: Why the way to it is closed?

resource.words: an open way to the kitchen

text: The way to the kitchen was already closed at the start: closed(kitchen) comes from the base state (#init), and no event since then produced it or changed it. When you asked me to go to the kitchen, go_closed[P=kitchen] (event 4) fired because the kitchen is mapped but not open. The world lacks open(kitchen), which the go move needs.

question: Why I am already busy with a task?

resource.words: being free of any other task (idle)

text: The find command for the keys was refused by find_busy (event 10) because the dog was still on its way to tag3. The go move at event 8 used up idle and left moving(tag3), and nothing has ended that trip since. The search move needs idle, so the dog said it was already busy with a task.

question: Why there is a wall right there?
text: The wall behind the dog was there from the start: wall(backward) is in the base state, and no event put it there. When the dog was told to move backward at event 14, it refused with move_wall because the world has wall(backward) and lacks clear(backward). Only clear(forward) holds.

question: Why it is locked away?
text: The dog's model has no reason for the extinguisher being locked away. The fact locked_away(extinguisher) came in from outside as a report (intervention 19), and no rule produces it. The dog only reacts to it: it was searching for the extinguisher, and find_locked (event 20) stopped the search with "I can't reach it: it is locked away."

question: Why it is not something I can or may do?
text: Event 26 fired the move unknown ("I can't do that: it is not something I can or may do."), which left refused(unknown). Its only requirement is the command token cmd_unknown, which event 25 added to the world. Nothing the world lacked caused this: the dog refuses any command classed as unknown, so no card explains it as a missing resource.

question: Why the battery is too low to search?
text: The dog refused the search (find_low[T=bottle], event 30) because battery_low holds and battery_ok is absent. battery_low was set by event 29 from outside the dog's moves; none of the dog's moves produces battery_ok, so nothing it can do restores the charge. The search needs the battery to be ok, and the world lacks that.

question: Why I have to stand up first?
text: You asked me to turn left, but I am sitting: the state shows posture(sitting). Turning needs me to be standing, so event 34, turn_must_stand[S=left,P=sitting], refused the turn. Tell me to stand first, then ask me to turn again.

question: The farmer carries the goat across first. Right after that crossing, on which bank are the farmer, the wolf, the goat and the cabbage?
expect: farmer far, goat far, wolf near, cabbage near
text: After firing carry[A=near,X=goat,B=far], state shows farmer(far) and on(goat,far) on the far bank, and on(wolf,near) and on(cabbage,near) still on the near bank. Nothing was eaten: there is no gone atom. The boat token was used up and landed is present, so the turn move must fire before the next trip.

question: In this session the cabbage is gone. Why was it eaten?
expect: #1 carry[wolf near→far] left the goat with the cabbage on the near bank, the farmer away; #3 eat[Y=cabbage,X=goat]: the goat ate the cabbage
text: The cabbage was eaten by the scripted eat move at event 3, eat[Y=cabbage,A=near,X=goat,B=far]: the goat and the cabbage were both on the near bank and the farmer was on the far bank. That happened because event 1, carry[A=near,X=wolf,B=far], took the wolf across first, and the tide (event 2) then let the banks settle. No resource was missing, and the answer kinds offered (missing or unexplained) do not cover an event the script itself predicts, so I report it as unexplained.

question: What if the farmer carries the cabbage across first instead of the goat? Does anything get eaten, and by what?
expect: the wolf eats the goat on the near bank (gone(goat))

question: In this session the cabbage is gone. Was carrying the wolf across first necessary for that?
expect: partly necessary: PN ≈ 0.8333 (P(gone(cabbage)) without #1 = 0.1667, by chance 0.375)
text: Carrying the wolf across first (event 1, carry[A=near,X=wolf,B=far]) was partly necessary for gone(cabbage), with PN ≈ 0.8333. With that trip blocked, the cabbage is gone in only 0.1667 of the re-run futures, against 0.375 by chance from the start. Taking the wolf left the goat and cabbage alone on the near bank, so event 3 eat[Y=cabbage,A=near,X=goat,B=far] could fire. Nothing was missing; the typed kinds don't fit a necessity question, so this is marked unexplained.
